content: Terconazole 8% Cream: Administer one full applicator of the cream intravaginally at bedtime for three consecutive days. Terconazole Suppository: Insert one suppository (80 mg) intravaginally at bedtime for three consecutive days. Safety and Efficacy: The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been fully established. Potential Side Effects: Common side effects include headache, abdominal pain, chills, fever, dysmenorrhea (painful menstruation), vulvar or vaginal burning, itching, soreness, swelling (edema), or discharge. Other possible side effects include increased urination (polyuria), burning or itching of the penis in a sexual partner, and flu-like symptoms. General Reactions: Some patients may experience asthenia (weakness), influenza-like illness (including fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, muscle pain, joint pain, and malaise). Immune System Reactions: Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and facial swelling (edema), have been reported. Nervous System Reactions: Dizziness may occur. Respiratory Reactions: Bronchospasm has been reported. Skin Reactions: Rash, toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), and urticaria (hives) may occur. Important Warnings: Discontinue use immediately if irritation or sensitization occurs. If the patient does not respond to terconazole treatment, repeat microbiological studies (e.g., KOH smear or cultures) to rule out other pathogens. Cases of anaphylaxis and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) have been reported. Discontinue the medication if these conditions develop and do not restart therapy. This product is petroleum-based and may damage latex or rubber condoms and diaphragms. Avoid using these contraceptive devices during treatment and for three days after completing treatment. Pregnancy and Lactation: This medication is classified as Pregnancy Category C. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed, and discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Pregnant women should exercise caution when using the vaginal applicator. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. The manufacturer does not recommend using this product during the first trimester of pregnancy. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Absorption and Excretion: Systemic absorption after vaginal administration may vary depending on the presence of a uterus. Women who have undergone a hysterectomy may absorb 5-8% of the medication, while non-hysterectomy women may absorb 12-16%. The medication is excreted through feces and urine. How to Use: This product is for vaginal use only. Wash your hands before and after use. Avoid contact with your eyes. If the medication gets into your eyes, rinse them thoroughly with water. Use the medication as directed by your doctor, typically once daily at bedtime for three or seven days, depending on the product. If using the cream, use the applicator provided. If using the suppository, you may use either the applicator or your finger for insertion. Unwrap the suppository before use. Follow the package instructions for filling the applicator with cream or inserting the suppository. Lie on your back with your knees bent toward your chest. Insert the applicator or suppository into the vagina as far as it will comfortably go. Slowly press the plunger of the applicator to release the medication. Clean the applicator with warm, soapy water, rinse well, and dry. Continue using the medication every day until the full prescribed amount is finished, even if symptoms improve after one or two days. This product can be used during menstruation. Do not use tampons or douches while using this medication. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Storage: Store the cream or suppository at room temperature. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to terconazole, other azole antifungal agents (e.g., clotrimazole, fluconazole), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Consult your doctor about whether you can engage in sexual intercourse while using this product. The suppository form (but not the cream) may damage rubber products such as latex condoms, diaphragms, or cervical caps, potentially leading to contraceptive failure and pregnancy. Avoid using these products during treatment and for three days after completing treatment. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Prevention of Vaginal Yeast Infections: To help prevent vaginal yeast infections, thoroughly dry the genital area after showering, bathing, or swimming. Avoid wearing tight jeans, nylon underwear, pantyhose, wet bathing suits, or damp/sweaty exercise clothes for extended periods. Important Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other infections unless directed by your doctor. If your condition does not improve or if it returns within two months, inform your doctor.
